items.title: Multi-level collaborative fault diagnosis and self-healing framework for proton exchange membrane fuel cell
items.abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) represent a key technology for energy transition, yet their reliability and lifespan are severely constrained by multi-source coupled failures. Current research predominantly focuses on isolated fault diagnosis or localized mitigation strategies, lacking a systematic governance framework to achieve closed-loop management from sensing to healing. This paper aims to address this challenge by systematically reviewing recent advances in fault diagnosis and self-healing strategies, proposing a forward-looking Hierarchical Collaborative Healing Framework (HCHF). First, it establishes a unified classification system integrating three major failure sources: the stack, sensors, and actuators. Subsequently, it comprehensively reviews model-based, signal processing, and data-driven diagnostic methods, comparing their respective advantages and limitations. Building upon this foundation, the core contribution is the HCHF framework, which organizes healing strategies into three synergistic tiers: (1) in-situ self-repair at the material and component level; (2) active fault-tolerant control at the system level; and (3) predictive health management at the system level. This framework enables cross-scale collaborative governance—from micro-level damage repair to macro-level system performance optimization—through a closed-loop interaction of diagnosis, decision-making, and healing. Finally, future research directions are explored by integrating cutting-edge trends such as digital twins and federated learning. This framework provides a systematic theoretical blueprint for the paradigm shift of PEMFC from “passive maintenance” to “active self-healing,” offering significant guidance for advancing the development of highly reliable fuel cell systems.

items.title: Profitability and carbon footprint of battery recycling and the potential impact on battery cost: A structured machine-learning based review
items.abstract: The rapid growth of the battery industry and the resulting battery waste feedstock as well as geopolitical dependencies and potential impending material shortages all necessitate a ramping ramp-up of the battery recycling industry. Among the various recycling processes, which can be classified into pyro, hydro, and direct recycling processes, no standard process has yet been established. In addition, the industry must adapt to the future battery technologies because of the impressive speed of development in battery technologies. Choosing the right combination of recycling process and battery technology is crucial for optimizing the profitability and sustainability of battery recycling. Considering this, we conducted a machine-learning-based systematic review to identify research gaps and analyze the Profitability and carbon footprint of pyro, hydro, and direct recycling for various battery technologies. We identified nickel and cobalt as key factors influencing the profitability and carbon footprint of battery recycling. Due to extended producer responsibility in many regions, recycling can reduce costs for nickel- and cobalt-rich batteries by up to 6 % in a circular economy, while nickel- and cobalt-free technologies may see a cost increase of around 5 % due to unprofitable recycling.

items.title: Recent progress in state of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries: From laboratory to practical application
items.abstract: The rapid development of electric vehicles and smart grids has posed severe challenges to the safety management of lithium-ion batteries. As an important indicator of battery aging and safety, the estimation of state of health (SOH) is crucial. Although SOH estimation methods have been fully developed, there is still a large gap between laboratory verification and practical application. This paper presents a systematic review of SOH estimation methods for lithium-ion batteries in recent years. Starting from the perspective of health indicators (HI), it attempts to find a reliable transition scheme between laboratory and practical applications. The current methods are summarized as geometric, statistical, parametric HIs based and methods without HI. Through literature analysis, it is found that statistical HIs show great potential in practical applications. In addition, the key technologies to bridge the gap between the two scenarios are also summarized, as well as the challenges and prospects of future SOH estimation, in the hope of providing unique insights for the realization of advanced SOH estimation methods in practical applications.

items.title: Seasonal borehole thermal energy storage for zero-carbon city heating: Mechanisms, optimization, and application challenges
items.abstract: Cold-climate city heating sector faces increasing pressure to reduce carbon emissions, highlighting the need for a zero-carbon, efficient, and economical solution. Borehole thermal energy storage (BTES) is one of the most promising thermal energy storage technologies to meet the demands. However, it faces challenges such as extended storage cycles, significant thermal inertia, and low energy density. This review provides an overview of recent advances in BTES across multiple scales, covering heat transfer mechanisms, design optimization, system integration, and engineering applications. First, the development of heat transfer models is summarized, with a focus on computational cost, simulation accuracy, and reliable performance. The heat loss of BTES systems has a decisive impact on storage performance, influenced primarily by system scale, soil thermal conductivity, and operating temperature difference, and can be mitigated through optimized system design and geological assessment. Furthermore, heating systems integrating BTES should consider the characteristics of heat sources and application scenarios to define suitable operation modes. Reported large-scale engineering applications demonstrate the strong climatic adaptability and potential of BTES, with storage efficiencies ranging from 19% to 63%. Finally, we propose a high-efficiency BTES design framework and identify research priorities for system-level integration into district heating networks.

This review aims to provide a systematic reference for the future development of photovoltaic window technology and to offer both theoretical support and practical insights for advancing building energy efficiency and green sustainable development.

It highlights recent developments in chamber design geometry but gives greater emphasis on turbine performance enhancement along with control system optimization. Self-rectifying air turbines, especially Wells turbine, Impulse turbine and their advanced variants with discussion of their aerodynamic efficiency, stall mitigation, and hybrid configurations have gained special focus. In terms of control, the review explores and critically examines the transition from traditional PID-based strategies to more robust control techniques such as Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Adaptive Proportional-Integral-Derivative (Adaptive PID), and Adaptive Model Predictive Control (AMPC) under nonlinear and irregular wave conditions. Rather than offering a historical summary, this review prioritizes recent research contributions, performance analysis and emerging techniques inthe turbine and control side, with necessary technical explanation. A key outcome of this review is the identification of unresolved challenges in turbine-chamber interaction, airflow losses due to blade tip clearance and vortex effects, optimizing stall mitigation technique, lack of established complex models, and real-time control strategies to completely omit chattering. While specifying the open challenges, this paper also outlines potential research directions including geometry-control co-optimization and adaptive strategies under non-linear wave conditions, as outcome. By accumulating recent findings, this review offers a technical roadmapfor guiding the next generation of high-efficiency, real time adaptive OWC technologies under real sea conditions.

items.title: Vibration of blades and towers in large offshore and floating wind turbines: Mechanisms, modelling credibility and mitigation pathways
items.abstract: The upscaling of wind turbines (WTs) and the expansion of offshore and floating deployment are turning blade and tower vibration from a component-level structural response into a system-level reliability issue. Longer and more flexible blades, taller towers, reduced modal frequencies and platform-induced motions increase blade–tower–support coupling and make vibration prediction more sensitive to modelling assumptions. This review examines blade and tower vibrations in large offshore and floating WTs using a mechanism-informed framework. Six vibration categories are considered: buffeting, periodic and parametric excitation, stall-related self-excited vibration, classical flutter, vortex-induced vibration (VIV), and resonance or modal interaction. For each category, observable vibration signatures are linked to dominant energy pathways, structural degrees of freedom and operating conditions. Modelling approaches are evaluated according to the physical quantities they must capture credibly, including load statistics, phase relationships, time-periodic coefficients, aerodynamic damping, vortex lock-in, modal frequencies and uncertainty bounds. Mitigation strategies are organised by mechanism-specific intervention pathways, including added damping, frequency management, aerodynamic or surface modification, flow-disruption devices, and control or operational measures. Their engineering trade-offs are discussed in terms of power production, load redistribution, offshore accessibility, reliability, maintenance and life-cycle cost are discussed. Future priorities include floating-platform-induced coupling, mechanism-specific validation benchmarks, uncertainty-aware stability and fatigue assessment, digital twins, and life-cycle reliability of mitigation systems.

items.title: Wind turbine blade damage: A systematic review of detection, diagnosis, performance impact, and lifecycle health management
items.abstract: Wind turbine blades (WTBs) are critical components that significantly influence energy capture efficiency and operational safety. However, they face diverse damage mechanisms in harsh environments, resulting in maintenance costs exceeding 20% of revenue for offshore installations. While various condition monitoring technologies exist, current research lacks integration, focusing on individual technologies without providing a comprehensive health management framework. Moreover, the quantitative mechanisms linking damage to performance degradation remain poorly understood, hindering effective predictive maintenance. This systematic review addresses these gaps by introducing a novel lifecycle health management (LCHM) framework that links damage mechanisms to proactive decision-making. Central to this framework is a hierarchical damage identification system comprising two progressive tiers: (1) damage detection, which determines the presence of anomalies, and (2) damage diagnosis, which localizes, classifies, and quantifies severity. Through critical comparison of widely used monitoring methods, applicable scenarios, limitations, and complementary strengths are identified. Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis of quantitative impact mechanisms is provided, demonstrating how different damage types affect aerodynamic efficiency, structural integrity, and power generation. Economic modeling reveals that implementing early proactive repair strategies can reduce lifecycle costs by up to 15% compared to traditional reactive approaches. The article concludes with a discussion of ongoing research challenges and prospects, highlighting promising future trends.

items.title: Wind turbine noise: A review of measurement, modeling and mitigation strategies
items.abstract: This review provides a structured and comprehensive analysis of wind turbine noise, covering the full chain from sound generation to measurement, modeling, and mitigation. Aerodynamic and mechanical noise sources are examined alongside their spectral and temporal characteristics and their implications for human perception. Standardized acoustic metrics and measurement procedures, including IEC 61400–11 and ISO 9613-2, are discussed in the context of field and wind-tunnel methodologies. The paper further reviews experimental and computational approaches, including semi-empirical models and high-fidelity simulations based on Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Computational Aeroacoustics (CAA), highlighting their capabilities and limitations for noise prediction. Existing mitigation strategies are analyzed, with emphasis on passive solutions such as aerodynamic blade modifications, porous materials, and vibration-damping systems. Despite significant progress, current approaches remain predominantly passive and often involve trade-offs with aerodynamic performance. A critical gap is identified in the limited development of active noise mitigation strategies, particularly for small and micro wind turbines operating in proximity to residential environments. While active control systems are widely used for power optimization, their application to aeroacoustic noise reduction remains largely unexplored. This review highlights the need for integrated methodologies combining measurement, modeling, and control, and outlines future directions toward adaptive, multidisciplinary solutions aimed at improving acoustic performance, social acceptance, and sustainable deployment of wind energy systems.

items.title: Advances in Hyperspectral Imaging for Spoilage Detection in Meat and Poultry: A Non-Invasive Approach
items.abstract:
Background
Meat and poultry are among the most highly perishable food commodities, and their rapid deterioration presents significant challenges to food safety, quality assurance, and economic sustainability. Conventional spoilage detection methods, including microbiological and chemical assays, remain reliable; however, they are often destructive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for real-time monitoring applications.
Scope and approach
Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) has become a prospective non-invasive technology that could be used in the simultaneous spatial and spectral data collection of the meat surface, offering in-depth information on chemical and microbial transformations. The present review is based on the current use of HSI in the process of monitoring microbial activity, identifying chemical indicators, including total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), Thiobarbituric Acid Reactive Substances (TBARS), and pH changes, and measuring visible changes in colour and texture. Special attention is given to the combination of HSI and chemometric methods and state-of-the-art machine learning models, such as principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), long short-term memory networks (LSTMs), and autoencoders.
Key findings and conclusion
HSI has proven to be very accurate in the early detection of spoilage, in most instances better than conventional means. New innovations, including creation of portable HSI units, artificial intelligence, and multimedia systems that combine HSI and other sensors or internet of things, have expanded its application potential. Nevertheless, there are still notable issues, such as managing massive amounts of data, high prices of equipment, and the lack of uniform protocols to implement in industries. Future studies must aim at minimizing the size of the devices, creation of strong calibration systems, and the ease of incorporation into smart food devices. Together, these developments make HSI a future-proof, non-destructive, and dependable technology to assess the quality and safety of modern meat. This review further demonstrates that hybrid VIS-NIR-SWIR configurations combined with interpretable chemometric and machine-learning models consistently outperform single-range systems, while the lack of standardized validation and regulatory frameworks remains the primary barrier to large-scale industrial adoption.

items.title: Advances in plant-based superoxide dismutase extraction: Insights into sources, extraction methods, purification systems, machine-learning optimization, and future directions
items.abstract:
Background
Plant-based SOD has emerged as a key subject in modern research, mainly because of its critical function in reducing oxidative stress and its use in food, pharmaceutical, and biomedical industries. The rising interest in natural antioxidants has accelerated efforts to identify plant sources rich in SOD and to enhance its extraction using advanced technologies.
Scope and approach
This review highlights recent advances in extracting and purifying Plant-based SOD for industrial applications. It covers conventional methods, buffer-assisted extraction, and green technologies, including ultrasonic, enzymatic, pulsed electric field, high-pressure, and hybrid approaches that preserve the enzyme's activity. The advantages, limitations, and practical challenges of each method are evaluated. Due to SOD's sensitivity and the demand for process automation, machine-learning (ML)-assisted and intelligent extraction strategies are emphasized. Finally, it discusses future research and practical applications of SOD in developing bioactive food products.
Key findings and conclusion
The review indicates that plants are a valuable source for SOD extraction, highlighting the importance of accurate quantification and the selection of economically feasible sources. Within the spectrum of novel technologies, hybrid methods such as ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction appear to be the most practical choice due to their cost efficiency and well-established industrial implementation. High-purity SOD can be obtained using chromatographic methods, with its purity easily determined through electrophoresis and SOD assay kits, and predictable using ML-assisted techniques. Future research should focus on scalable, cost-efficient methods, sustainable sourcing, thorough enzyme characterization, and process standardization to fully unlock the Plant-based SOD therapeutic and industrial potential.

items.title: Anti-melanogenic bioactive peptides: Molecular mechanisms, source, preparation, structural optimization and cross-field prospective application
items.abstract:
Background
Abnormal melanin deposition causes skin hyperpigmentation disorders and enzymatic browning in food products, seriously affecting human health and food quality. Tyrosinase is the core rate-limiting enzyme during melanin biosynthesis. However, obvious controversies exist in published studies concerning peptide structure–activity rules and modification parameter optimization. Unresolved obstacles including ambiguous pathway cross-regulation, unstable peptide performance and high manufacturing cost greatly hinder their industrial translation.
Scope and approach
Literatures were retrieved from Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed and ScienceDirect using combined keywords related to anti-melanogenic bioactive peptides, covering publications from 2015 to early 2025 with key earlier classics supplemented. This review adopts comparative analysis, cross-disciplinary collation and structure-activity correlation sorting as core analytical approaches to critically synthesize literatures. We contrast multi-path inhibitory mechanisms, classify diverse natural sources, benchmark pros and cons of enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation and synthetic biology preparation, and dissect structure-function changes triggered by lipidation, glycosylation and cyclization. Meanwhile, conflicting experimental results from existing researches are summarized, and core unsolved scientific issues are sorted to connect basic peptide research with downstream whitening cosmetic and food anti-browning applications.
Key findings and conclusions
Bioactive peptides exhibit anti-melanogenic effects through multi-pathway regulation, including direct tyrosinase inhibition, signaling pathway modulation and melanosome transport interference. Preparation routes and structural modification directly determine peptide stability, permeability and bioavailability. This work prioritizes pending research gaps and proposes targeted developmental orientations for subsequent peptide design and scaled-up production. This review summarizes current challenges and future directions, providing a theoretical reference for the development and industrial translation of highly efficient and safe melanin-inhibitory peptides.

items.title: Effects of food processing on dietary protein quality: A systematic review, pairwise and network meta-analysis of in-vitro studies and randomised controlled trials
items.abstract:
Background
Processing is increasingly used to enhance functionality, palatability and nutritional quality of dietary protein. While processing is frequently associated with improved in-vitro protein digestibility, the magnitude and consistency of these effects vary across processing methods and protein sources. Moreover, it remains unclear whether in-vitro improvements translate into physiological human benefits, such as greater postprandial amino acid bioavailability and muscle anabolic responses. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically review and evaluate effects of diverse types of processing on protein quality, measured in both in-vitro and human clinical studies.
Scope and methods
A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL and Cochrane databases. Of 223 articles selected for systematic review, 62 and 22 were eligible for further pairwise and network meta-analysis respectively.
Key findings and conclusion
Processing consistently improved in-vitro protein digestibility [WMD: 7.96%, 95% CI: 6.94, 8.97] regardless of protein source. In human clinical studies, although no changes in iAUC of total amino acids or muscle fractional synthetic rates were noted, significant increases in Cmax (EAA) [WMD: 123.87 μmol/L, 95% CI: 54.10, 193.64] and Cmax (BCAA) [WMD: 55.73 μmol/L, 95% CI: 1.66, 109.79] were observed. Particularly, gelation and cold plasma demonstrated highest probabilities of improving Cmax (EAA) in network meta-analysis. Overall, processing improves in-vitro protein digestibility, but this does not consistently translate into greater systemic amino acid bioavailability or muscle utilisation in humans. Future processing strategies should move beyond in-vitro digestibility metrics to achieve meaningful physiological improvements.

items.title: Food protein-derived mineral binding peptides for mineral specific carrier design beyond chelation screening
items.abstract:
Background
Mineral binding by food protein-derived peptides is commonly interpreted as beneficial chelation. However, strong peptide-mineral association may either preserve an accessible mineral pool or immobilize essential minerals in poorly exchangeable complexes. Because apparent binding capacity alone confuses coordination stoichiometry with nutritional significance, mineral accessibility—the capacity to maintain soluble and exchangeable mineral species under realistic conditions—provides a more appropriate evaluation criterion. The central scientific issue is to distinguish peptide carriers from mineral sinks under food-processing and gastrointestinal conditions.
Scope and approach
This review reorganizes mineral-binding peptide research into a mineral-specific carrier-design framework. Accessibility is operationalized through conditional binding, soluble retention, matrix competition, and epithelial compatibility. Methodological coverage includes INFOGEST digestion with ICP-MS evaluation, EDTA/phytic acid competitive exchange for exchangeability assessment, and Caco-2 monolayer transport combined with bioavailability validation. Small-molecule chelators are used as chemical priors. Enzymatic preparation and fraction standardization are connected with the release of peptide motifs as food-source and ingredient development. AI-guided design is discussed through peptide-ion-condition records that integrate sequence features with mineral identity and assay context.
Key findings and conclusions
Calcium peptide systems are governed mainly by oxygen-donor motifs and precipitation control. Zinc peptide systems require mixed donor patterns and resistance to phytate displacement. Iron peptide systems require pH-dependent solubility and redox compatibility. Enzymatic production should preserve ion-adapted motifs and generate standardized fractions. AI models require mineral-specific descriptors rather than generic peptide-activity labels. This framework shifts the field from empirical chelation screening toward mechanism-informed, process-compatible mineral-carrier design.

items.title: From gut to whole body: Natural polysaccharide-based multi-axis network strategies for systemic disease adjuvant therapy
items.abstract:
Background
Natural polysaccharides are bioactive macromolecules that regulate gut-derived multi-axis networks, offering systemic therapeutic potential. Their structural diversity enables modulation of microbial, immune, neural and metabolic pathways. As gut dysbiosis is increasingly linked to systemic diseases, understanding polysaccharide-mediated gut-organ axis regulation has become crucial for developing novel interventions targeting systemic disease.
Scope and approach
This review examines polysaccharide mechanisms in microbiota modulation, barrier repair, and cross-organ communication via neural (vagus nerve), immune (Th17/Treg) and metabolic (SCFAs, bile acids) pathways. We analyze therapeutic applications across gut-brain, gut-lung, gut-liver, gut-kidney, gut-mammary, gut-bone, gut-skin, and gut-muscle axes, as well as chemical modifications (sulfation, carboxymethylation, selenylation, acetylation) that enhance bioactivity. The integration of multi-omics and precision engineering for next-generation polysaccharide drug development is also explored.
Key findings and conclusions
Polysaccharides restore gut homeostasis and exert systemic effects, alleviating neurodegenerative diseases (gut-brain), respiratory diseases (gut-lung), hepatic disorders (gut-liver), renal disorders (gut-kidney), mammary disorders (gut-mammary), skeletal disorders (gut-bone), dermatological disorders (gut-skin), and exercise-induced fatigue (gut-muscle). Chemical modifications optimize targeting and efficacy. Multi-omics approaches enable precision engineering of polysaccharide therapeutics. These findings position gut-centric polysaccharide regulation as a transformative strategy for systemic diseases, with optimized structures and systems biology approaches unlocking their full clinical potential across multiple organ system.

items.title: Indices for food classification systems: A perspective from food technology, nutrition, and beyond
items.abstract:
Background
Classification systems (FCSs) are widely used to categorize foods based on selected indices and to derive dietary guidelines. Recently, there has been controversy over the robustness of FCSs and the NOVA classification of ultra-processed foods (UPFs).
Scope and approach
This review presents and discusses indices within a framework comprising fresh or natural foods, prepared and processed foods (PFPs), and UPFs. Indices were grouped by formulation, processing, or socio-economic and environmental factors.
Key findings and conclusions
Indices based on food composition databases and nutrient content are influenced by data quality, food variability, analytical imprecision, and the absence of matrix-effect considerations. Processing indices, usually associated with unit operations, require additional criteria to assess their relevance and weight within the overall process. Indicators for “natural processing” are introduced to account for storage, spontaneous fermentations, and post-cooking events at the time of consumption. It was confirmed that some indices behind UPFs are often ill-defined (e.g., palatability). Nutrient bioavailability and the glycemic index of starchy foods provide valuable insights into the effects of formulation and processing. It is proposed that current FCSs be attentive to emerging trends in sustainability and people's well-being by incorporating indices for food security, socio-cultural conditions, and food waste, thereby adopting a more holistic approach. Developing scientifically based and validated indices to classify foods would guide consumers in making sustainable, healthy food choices and provide policymakers with robust information for their dietary recommendations.

items.title: Promise versus Proof: Can hyperspectral imaging move beyond proof-of-concept for foodborne pathogen detection?
items.abstract:
Background
Compliance with food safety standards is central to managing financial and reputational risks in food manufacturing, which in turn drives demand for rapid pathogen detection. Near-infrared hyperspectral imaging (NIR-HSI), the combination of near-infrared spectroscopy and imaging, has emerged as a promising, rapid, non-destructive tool for detecting foodborne pathogens and differentiating genera, species, and serotypes on a range of matrices.
Scope and approach
This review critically evaluates the evidence for NIR-HSI in pathogen detection, from fundamental spectroscopic principles to practical implementation. It summarises current applications on agar, smears and foods, compares NIR-HSI with established culture, PCR, ELISA and MALDI-TOF methods and examines chemometric and deep-learning approaches for data analysis.
Key findings and conclusions
Across published studies, informative bands are concentrated in the visible region of visible near-infrared (VNIR) instruments. However, the underlying biochemical mechanisms remain poorly defined, undermining confidence in the technique's robustness under real-world conditions. Most models are built on small, homogeneous datasets often with limited microbiological realism, incomplete validation against reference methods and little assessment of robustness across matrices, instruments or mixed microbial communities.
Significance and novelty
Within the landscape of rapid pathogen testing, this review outlines how clarifying the mechanistic basis of spectral fingerprints, integrating deep learning with interpretable chemometrics and standardising validation and reporting could move NIR-HSI beyond proof-of-concept. It also identifies realistic near-term niches, such as sample triage and serotype-oriented screening in high-throughput laboratories, where NIR-HSI could offer practical benefits, given current technological constraints.

items.title: Recent advances in biomimetic fusion strategies for multi-source heterogeneous data in food detection and safety assessment: A critical review
items.abstract:
Background:
The global food safety crisis and strict traceability demands require integrating complex data obtained using diverse sensors across the supply chain. While artificial intelligence has propelled multi-source fusion, traditional models often struggle to adapt to dynamic real-world environments. To tackle these challenges, biomimetic fusion strategies offer a highly flexible and robust solution. By mimicking biological processes and continuously learning from new information, they effectively integrate complex data obtained from various detection techniques.
Scope and approach:
Herein, we review recent advances in biomimetic fusion strategies for obtaining multi-source heterogeneous data in food detection. We first categorize sensing data into structured and high-dimensional unstructured data. Guided by the computational intelligence evolution, we analyze the complementary progression, dataset adaptability of three fusion modes: (i) fixed-pattern fusion, which enables efficient and stable integration but has limited flexibility; (ii) dynamic-pattern fusion, which enables context-aware adaptation but incurs greater computational complexity; and (iii) active-pattern fusion, which supports autonomous, goal-directed exploration but faces training instability and environmental dependence. Three mechanisms highlight a synergistic evolution from passive aggregation to intelligent exploration. Finally, by summarizing representative food applications, we highlight future research directions for overcoming key bottlenecks in task-oriented sensor coordination, complex matrix adaptability, resource-efficient active sensing, closed-loop detection, real-world domain shift, and interpretable fusion decision-making.
Key findings and conclusions:
Biomimetic fusion strategies show immense potential for enhancing food detection accuracy and decision autonomy. By leveraging complementary fixed, dynamic, and active patterns, these strategies drive a paradigm shift from passive aggregation toward active information acquisition. Their applicable boundaries depend primarily on task stability, the need for adaptive representation, and the feasibility of interactive sensing: fixed-pattern fusion is preferred for standardized detection tasks with stable acquisition conditions; dynamic-pattern fusion is more appropriate when fusion relationships must adapt to sample, sensor, or environmental variations; and active-pattern fusion is suitable for open or uncertain scenarios in which the system can iteratively acquire additional information to support decision-making. Across these application boundaries, challenges such as complex food matrices, sensor drift, weak or localized hazards, and limited model interpretability remain. Future advances in uncertainty-driven active sensing, closed-loop feedback, edge computing, digital twins, and lightweight algorithms are expected to support more trustworthy food safety supervision.

items.title: Recent advances in spray drying of plant-based dairy substitute powders: process optimization and quality outcomes
items.abstract:
Background
The increasing demand for plant-based dairy substitute powders (PBDSPs) has created a requirement for stable, high-quality products in the market. Spray drying is widely used in this context, offering benefits to both consumers and manufacturers. However, the compositional variability of plant-based matrices poses significant challenges during spray drying, particularly in maintaining the structural and functional integrity of the resulting PBDSPs.
Aim and method
This systematic review synthesizes findings from 47 peer-reviewed research studies, published in English between 2010 and 2025, on spray drying of PBDSPs. Those articles were retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases. This covers process optimization, formulation strategies, quality, and stability aspects.
Key findings and conclusions
Key process parameters, including inlet and outlet air temperatures, feed flow rate, atomization and airflow conditions, feed solid concentration, and carrier selection, have been identified as critical variables influencing PBDSP quality and stability. The findings revealed that the structural and functional integrity of the spray-dried PBDSPs is governed by interactions between processing conditions and plant-based composition, necessitating material-specific optimization strategies. Formulation modifications, carrier optimization, and process control are identified as effective strategies. However, key challenges remain, such as limited scalability beyond laboratory studies and insufficient understanding of structure-function relationships. This review addresses these gaps by systematically analyzing the interactions between formulation and processing, providing a basis for stable, high-quality PBDSP production. Future research should explore efficient pretreatments, formulation strategies, pilot-scale validation, and environmental impact assessments to move from laboratory studies to industrial applications.

items.title: Recent advances in the discovery, heterologous expression, protein engineering, and immobilization of cellobiose 2-epimerases
items.abstract:
Background
The dual challenges of lactose intolerance and environmental pollution from whey disposal necessitate the efficient valorization of lactose. Cellobiose 2-epimerases (CEases) have emerged as promising biocatalysts for converting lactose into high-value functional sugars, specifically lactulose and epilactose.
Scope and approach
This review provides a comprehensive overview of the microbial sources, biochemical characteristics, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of CEases. Furthermore, it critically analyzes recent advancements in enhancing enzymatic performance through structure-guided dynamic engineering, improving operational stability via innovative carrier-free and nano-matrix immobilization technologies, and optimizing scalable production using GRAS microbial hosts and dynamic control systems.
Key findings and conclusions
CEases have demonstrated great potential in the dairy industry and the synthesis of functional sugars. Advancements in AI-assisted mining have significantly accelerated the discovery of novel candidates. Mechanistically, computational breakthroughs have advanced our understanding from foundational epimerization to a dynamic “swaying mechanism” governing the dual activities of bifunctional CEases. Building on these mechanistic insights, the rational engineering of structural dynamics has significantly improved CEase catalytic efficiency and product selectivity. Moreover, the transition to GRAS expression systems enables safe, food-grade production. Future research should further integrate computational biology with robust, heavy-metal-free immobilization platforms to establish scalable, zero-waste biocatalytic processes for the functional sugar industry.

items.title: The convergence of food-derived bioactive peptides and organoids: model construction, application, challenges and outlooks
items.abstract:
Background
Food-derived bioactive peptides (FBPs) are increasingly recognized for diverse functional benefits. However, current mainstream evaluation methods, such as in vitro biochemical experiments, 2D cell cultures and animal models, inherently lack the physiological complexity and human relevance necessary to accurately simulate the intricate in vivo environment, thereby creating a bottleneck in understanding FBPs' authentic mechanisms of action and predicting their efficacy.
Scope and approach
To address the gap, an overview of FBP sources, key activities, and molecular mechanisms was provided in this review. Subsequently, the construction protocols and major types of current organoid technology were introduced, with particular emphasis placed on their unique advantages. Furthermore, the application potential and associated challenges of organoid models in FBP research were thoroughly explored.
Key findings and conclusions
Given the significant regulatory roles played by FBPs in various physiological activities such as anti-inflammation, antioxidation, and osteogenesis, and with the continuous advancement of organoid research targeting the gut, brain, bone, and other organs, organoid models are considered instrumental in achieving a deeper understanding of FBP digestion, absorption, and bioaccessibility. However, this field still faces numerous challenges, including insufficient technical standardization, the lack of complete vascular and immune systems, and high production costs. Therefore, the integration of organoid technology with organ-on-a-chip platforms to enable multi-organ interaction, the introduction of multi-lineage co-cultures to enhance biological complexity, and the utilization of artificial intelligence and multi-omics analysis for data integration are regarded as key directions for promoting the industrial translation of organoid technology in FBP research.

This effect provides a theoretical basis for understanding excellent properties of perovskite-type anodes and offers new insights for rational designing next-generation high-performance anode materials.

items.title: Confined microenvironments induced by tri-anion fluorinated polymer network enable localized disordered solvation for high-voltage quasi-solid-state lithium metal batteries
items.abstract:
Quasi-solid electrolytes hold promise for high-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs), yet their practical application is limited by sluggish Li+ transport and unstable interphases. Herein, a tri-anion quasi-solid electrolyte (TA-FPE) with an in situ fluorinated polymer network is developed to engineer confined microenvironments and regulate electrolyte chemistry. The electron-withdrawing -CF3 groups weaken Li+-solvent interactions, while the coexistence of FSI-, DFOB-, BF4-, and multiple solvents broadens the distribution of local Li+ coordination environments, inducing local solvation disorder. Spectroscopic and computational analyses reveal that the locally disordered solvation environment, confined by the fluorinated polymer network, promotes anion participation in the Li+ solvation sheath, lowering the desolvation barrier and accelerating charge-transfer kinetics. This environment promotes robust LiF- and B-O-rich interphases, stabilizing both lithium metal and high-voltage cathodes. Consequently, TA-FPE exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.50 mS cm-1, a Li+ transference number (𝑡+
𝐿⁢𝑖) of 0.71, and an oxidation stability up to 4.6 V. It enables stable cycling of Li||LFP and Li||NCM811 cells, including high-loading cathodes under limited-lithium conditions. Furthermore, stable cycling is achieved in graphite and lithium metal pouch cells, with the latter delivering an energy density exceeding 350 Wh kg-1. This work highlights local solvation disorder as an effective strategy for high-voltage quasi-solid-state LMBs.

items.title: Decoding silicon-driven degradation: An adaptive fusion framework for robust battery electrode-level diagnostics
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) with silicon-containing composite anodes offer higher energy density, but their multi-physics coupled degradation mechanisms, compounded by stochastic operating conditions and diverse chemistries, present fundamental challenges to reliable holistic health estimation. In this study, we first in situ decouple the capacity contributions of silicon and graphite in blended electrode across the full lifespan, underscoring the significance of onboard disentangling the silicon capacity share for comprehensive health assessment and component-aware battery management. Consequently, we propose an adaptive charging segment and feature fusion bimodal network (ASEFNet) to capture accurate electrode-level degradation dynamics in silicon-containing LIBs. Specifically, the framework flexibly accommodates arbitrary dynamic charging conditions and leverages available relaxation information, thereby enhancing diagnostic precision and ensuring robust generalizability across different applications. The framework is evaluated on diverse cycling datasets spanning different electrode chemistries and operating protocols, with a mean absolute percentage error of <2% for electrode parameters estimation, highlighting the adaptive and versatile utility of the framework.

items.title: Design of interpenetrating-polymer network electrolytes for speedy Li+ transport and uniform Li-deposition in solid-state lithium batteries
items.abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) offer excellent electrode compatibility for solid-state batteries. Here, we develop a novel interpenetrating polymer network electrolyte (IPNE) based on polyethylene oxide (PEO) and polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), incorporating lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt and synthesized using high-polarity dimethylacetamide (DMAc) to enhance Li+ transport. To achieve high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability, CuF2 and LiNO3 additives are introduced, forming CL-IPNE membranes. These additives react with lithium to generate a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) enriched with LiF and Li3N, ensuring strong adhesion and uniform Li deposition. CuF2 reduction produces Cu0 nanoparticles that spatially separate SEI domains and create additional Li+ pathways, while Cu2+ in the bulk weakens Li+–polymer and Li+–solvent interactions, promoting mobility. Consequently, CL-IPNE exhibits an ionic conductivity of 1.3 mS cm−1 at 30 °C, and Li|CL-IPNE|LiFePO4 cells retain 87% capacity after 400 cycles of charge-discharge at 1.5 mA cm−2. The free-standing membranes are compatible with roll-to-roll processing, enabling scalable, cost-effective manufacturing. This work highlights the synergistic roles of CuF2 and LiNO3 in advancing SPE performance for high-energy solid-state batteries.

items.title: Double-network hybrid hydrogel electrolyte suppresses zinc dendrites and vanadium dissolution for durable zinc-metal batteries
items.abstract: Electrolytes are crucial for developing long-cycling and safe aqueous zinc-metal batteries (AZMBs), yet conventional liquid systems suffer from zinc (Zn) dendrite growth and hydrogen evolution. Herein, we design a double-network hydrogel electrolyte, denoted P(AM-co-AA)-CS by copolymerizing acrylamide and acrylic acid coordinated with chitosan. Unlike single-network polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogels, the P(AM-co-AA)-CS hydrogel exhibits good mechanical robustness under stretching, cutting, and knotting, along with rapid self-healing capability essential for resisting Zn dendrite penetration. The chitosan matrix reconstitutes the hydrogen-bond network, restricting water activity and suppressing parasitic reactions, thus enhancing Zn metal reversibility. Thus, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell achieves satisfactory cycle stability exceeding 3000 h, significantly outperforming the bare PAM-based cell (1800 h). The Zn//vanadium oxide (VO2) full cell also maintains high stability over 3000 cycles, attributed to the suppressed vanadium dissolution that verified by X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. A pouch cell assembled with the hydrogel demonstrates 120 stable cycles and can work normally under mechanical deformation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing multifunctional hydrogel electrolytes toward durable and high-safety AZMBs.

items.title: Dual anchoring via Lewis acid sites and hydrogen bonds enables synergistic performance optimization of lithium metal batteries
items.abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) hold immense promise for next-generation lithium metal batteries, yet their progress is fundamentally hampered by an intrinsic trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength, further exacerbated by uncontrolled anion migration. Herein, we report a rationally designed composite SPE that transcends these limitations through a synergistic dual-anchor strategy. By integrating lithium titanate (Li4Ti5O12, LTO) nanoparticles with two functional sites on their surface into a thermoplastic polyurethane/polycarbonate matrix, we create a multifunctional network. In this network, (i) Lewis-acidic Ti4+ sites on LTO selectively immobilize TFSI− anions, promoting LiTFSI dissociation and yielding a high lithium-ion transference number (tLi+) of 0.73, thereby suppressing space-charge layer effects; (ii) hydroxyl groups on LTO form dense hydrogen bonds with polymer carbonyls, constructing a robust framework that enhances tensile strength to 4.1 MPa without disrupting continuous ion-conduction pathways. This design enables the synergistic enhancement of ionic conductivity and mechanical properties, resulting in an exceptional ionic conductivity (1.26 mS cm−1) at 30 °C, a low activation energy (0.195 eV), and a wide electrochemical stability window (5.0 V). Consequently, the Li||Li symmetric cell demonstrates ultralong cycling stability over 1600 h at 0.5 mA cm−2. When paired with a LiFePO4 cathode, the full cell delivers outstanding rate capability and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 330 cycles at a high rate of 2 C. This work not only presents a high-performance SPE but also establishes a versatile design paradigm that leverages coupled Lewis-acidic and hydrogen-bonding interactions to overcome the long-standing strength-conductivity dilemma in solid-state electrolytes for dendrite-free lithium metal batteries.

items.title: Dual-network eutectogel electrolyte with enhanced interfacial stability for high-performance flexible zinc-air batteries
items.abstract: Conventional gel polymer electrolytes, plagued by poor interfacial stability and narrow operating temperature ranges, severely limit the performance of flexible zinc-air batteries (FZABs). Herein, we design a dual-network eutectogel electrolyte (PAAM) using a citric acid/ethylene glycol deep eutectic solvent (DES), with acrylic acid (AA) forming the first network and acrylamide (AM) forming the second interpenetrating network via radical polymerization. The cooperative hydrogen-bonding between amide and carboxyl groups create a dense three-dimensional polymer network, endowing PAAM with excellent mechanical performance, rapid self-healing ability, high ionic conductivity, and strong interfacial adhesion. Importantly, the dual-network structure provides physical confinement, while the DES supplies chemical confinement and abundant zincophilic functional groups. This synergy efficiently converts free water into bound water, suppressing hydrogen evolution and parasitic corrosion. Meanwhile, the uniform and continuous ion transport network adsorbs Zn(OH)42- species and guides homogeneous zinc deposition, efficiently preventing dendrite growth and passivation. Consequently, FZABs assembled with PAAM deliver a large open-circuit voltage of 1.39 V, a specific capacity of 808.8 mAh gZn-1, a peak power density of 255.33 mW cm-2, and a good cycling stability of 425 cycles. Moreover, the PAAM electrolyte enables stable operation of flexible devices from -40 to 130 °C. This work provides a promising dual-network eutectogel design strategy to simultaneously enhance interfacial stability and temperature adaptability for advanced FZABs.

items.title: Electron-delocalized π-network enables low-reactive polyacrylonitrile-based solid-state electrolytes for lithium metal batteries
items.abstract: As one of the most promising solid-state polymer electrolytes (SPEs), Polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based SPEs suffer from unstable interfaces due to their highly reactivity with lithium metal anode. Here, the molecular chain of the PAN polymer is tailored through surface-basicity-guided reactions of Li7La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 (LLZTO) and an electrostatic shielding effect of 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium cation (EMIM⁺), effectively mitigating its reactivity with Li. The alkalinity of LLZTO catalyze PAN dehydrocyanation, transforming –CN groups to π-conjugated –C=N/–C=C– bonds, thus decreasing its inherent reactivity with the Li metal. Then, the positive EMIM⁺ with an electron-delocalized π-network electrostatically connect with polarized –C=N sites, shielding the direct contact of –CN groups with Li, further alleviating parasitic reactions. As a result, the Li//Li symmetric cells deliver high critical current density of 3.0 mA cm−2 and maintain stable Li plating/stripping over 2000 h. The Li//LFP cell delivers a high capacity retention of 87.53 % after 1200 cycles at 2C, and the pouch battery presents excellent cycling and safety performance. This work provides a promising approach to enable the stable operation of solid-state lithium metal batteries via incorporating the electron-delocalized π-network.

items.title: From high-throughput discovery to molecular design principles of multi-redox lithium-ion organic cathodes
items.abstract: Multi-redox organic cathodes offer a promising route toward high-capacity, sustainable energy storage by enabling multiple sequential redox reactions. However, the development of these materials is hindered by conventional computational screening methods, which typically simplify the lithiation process and thus fail to accurately predict their key cathodic properties. To address this, we develop AutoVoltage, a computational workflow that automates the simulation of the complete sequential lithiation process, enabling a comprehensive and accurate prediction of cathodic properties. Applying our framework to a large-scale screening of the PubChem database, we identify 202 optimal candidates with outstanding specific energies exceeding 1000 Wh/kg. A subsequent data-driven analysis of these candidates reveals three distinct structural clusters: a functional cluster (FC), a polycyclic cluster (PC), and a branched cluster (BC). Our analysis establishes that distinct structural patterns govern key cathodic properties. The electron-withdrawing groups of the FC elevate voltage by creating an environment with reduced electron density, while the fused structures of the PC maximize capacity via high redox center density. Furthermore, the branched architecture of the BC promotes a low voltage slope through the structural separation of redox centers. This work provides not only a powerful screening methodology and a pool of high-performance materials but also a set of fundamental structural design principles for the rational development of next-generation organic cathodes.

items.title: Generalized capacity estimation for retired lithium-ion batteries: Unsupervised electrochemical impedance spectroscopy dimensionality reduction under random retirement conditions
items.abstract: The echelon utilization and material recycling of retired batteries offer significant economic benefits, yet their large-scale application remains hindered by time-consuming and inaccurate performance assessment. This study presents a novel approach that combines dimensionality-reduced electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) features with machine learning (ML) regression to address the challenges of capacity estimation in the absence of historical operational conditions and state of charge (SOC) calibration. By standardizing high-dimensional EIS data into 2-dimensional features through dimensionality reduction techniques, the proposed method effectively decouples aging-related information from retirement conditions. The extracted EIS features, when fed into ML regressors, demonstrate robust capacity estimation performance under unknown SOCs. A comprehensive validation is conducted using 6 distinct datasets comprising over 2500 EIS measurements, covering 3 cathode material compositions, 3 physical formats, and 6 capacity specifications. For laboratory-aged batteries subjected to accelerated aging protocols, the method achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 2.25% and 1.43%. Remarkably, it maintains high accuracy when applied to real-world retired batteries, yielding MAPEs of 4.63%, 1.94%, 1.53%, and 4.62% across 4 distinct retired battery datasets. This approach significantly reduces the testing time for capacity assessment from hours to minutes without compromising accuracy, providing an efficient and promising solution for large-scale retired battery performance evaluation.

items.title: Highly stable composite polymer electrolyte with covalent/non-covalent network for solid-state zinc-iodine battery
items.abstract: Zinc-iodine (Zn-I2) batteries have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems due to their low cost, environmental friendliness, and inherent safety. However, challenges such as Zn dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, and the shuttle effect of polyiodides in liquid electrolytes significantly hinder their practical applications. To address these issues, we propose a novel composite polymer electrolyte (CPE) with a dual-network design, integrating a 3D porous β-cyclodextrin polymer (CDP) framework and hollow spherical TiO2 (H-TiO2) nanoparticles through synergistic covalent/non-covalent interactions. The CDP is constructed by cross-linking flexible β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) units with rigid aryl-rich polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIM-1), forming a mechanically robust and highly porous architecture. Within this network, H-TiO2 nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed via hydrogen bonding with PEO chains and CDP functional groups, enhancing interfacial compatibility and ion transport pathways. The resulting electrolyte (PCPE-CDP-TiO2) achieves an exceptional ionic conductivity of 9.4 × 10–4 S cm-1 at room temperature, and effectively suppresses Zn dendrite growth and polyiodide shuttling. Symmetrical Zn//Zn batteries with PCPE-CDP-TiO2 exhibit reversible Zn plating/stripping for over 11,000 hours at 5 mA cm-2. Solid-state Zn-I2 full batteries enables an ultra-long cycle life of 10,000 cycles at 5 C. This work presents a molecular engineering strategy for designing high-performance CPEs.

items.title: Homogeneous solid electrolyte interphase network confines electrochemical sintering toward ultra-stable micro-silicon sulfide solid-state anodes
items.abstract: Micro-silicon (μSi) is a promising high-capacity anode material for sulfide solid-state lithium batteries; however, repeated lithiation/delithiation induces severe chemo-mechanical degradation, accompanied by electrode-scale full electrochemical sintering, localized stress concentration, crack propagation, and interfacial contact loss. Herein, we construct a homogeneous organic-inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase (H-SEI) network throughout the μSi electrode to enable confined electrochemical sintering via interphase engineering. Unlike conventional gradient SEI architectures, the interconnected H-SEI network simultaneously integrates high mechanical modulus and is proposed to promote interfacial interactions with both silicon and sulfide solid electrolyte. The homogeneous interphase reduces the formation of high-volume-expansion crystalline Li15Si4, redistributes lithiation-induced stress, and confines electrochemical sintering at the microparticle scale, preventing its propagation across the electrode. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed organic components maintain intimate and stable Si/LPSCl contact during long-term electrochemical cycling. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of electrochemical sintering and interfacial stability, the H-SEI-modified μSi electrode delivers a high areal capacity of 2.15 mAh cm-2, ultralong cycling stability over 1400 cycles with an ultralow average capacity decay rate of 0.032% per cycle, and excellent rate capability of 958 mAh g-1 at 8.75 A g-1. This work provides an effective interphase engineering strategy for regulating electrochemical sintering and chemo-mechanical evolution in micro-silicon anodes, offering new insights into the development of durable sulfide solid-state lithium batteries.

items.title: Model-informed design of microcrack-tolerant cathodes for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries
items.abstract: Boosting the fast-charging capability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for the widespread adoption of electric vehicles. However, nickel-rich layered oxides—the leading cathode materials for high-energy LIBs—suffer from microcracking during fast-charge cycling, resulting in severe capacity fading. Here, we propose an advanced design strategy for mechanically robust bimodal Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes guided by three-dimensional (3D) electrochemo-mechanical modeling. The 3D models, constructed with realistic particle morphologies and electrode microstructures, resolve the evolution of reaction heterogeneity and mechanical stress in the cathodes upon fast charging. Combined with experimental validation, we reveal that the dominant degradation pathway is microcracking of large cathode particles (diameter ∼12 µm) near the separator driven by coupled electrode- and particle-level reaction heterogeneity—namely, sluggish electrolyte-phase ionic transport in densely packed electrodes and diffusion limitation within large particles. To address these issues, we develop a bilayer cathode architecture featuring a ∼10 µm-thick top layer of small single-crystalline particles (∼3 µm). Due to their uniform small size and mechanical robustness, the single-crystalline particles enable fast, homogeneous reactions in the current-concentrated region near the separator and simultaneously act as a mechanical buffer that suppresses localized stress in the underlying large particles. As a result, the bilayer cathode effectively suppresses microcrack formation and subsequent parasitic reactions, delivering a high capacity retention of 76.2% after 300 cycles at 3C, compared with 62.4% for a conventional cathode. This work establishes a practical electrode design principle for enabling durable, high-energy, fast-charging LIBs.

items.title: Modulating the hydrogen-bond network via molecular crowding for high-voltage electrochemical stability in aqueous zinc batteries
items.abstract: In aqueous zinc batteries, the reactivity of water is intrinsically coupled with ion solvation and interfacial stability, limiting the operating voltages and long-term reversibility. Here, a molecular crowding electrolyte (MCE) is developed to reconfigure the hydrogen-bond network and Zn2+ solvation environment. We uncover a distinct mechanism in which the molecular crowding environment regulates water activity and weakens the H2OH2O hydrogen-bond network through physical localization without altering the primary Zn2+ solvation shell. The crowding agent self-associates outside the primary solvation shell, forming a crowding network that indirectly modulates solvation structure. The developed MCE delivers a Coulombic efficiency of 99.82% for 6600 cycles at 10 mA cm−2 and enables Zn plating/stripping 4000 h at 1 mA cm−2, 1 mAh cm−2. The MCE expands the electrochemical stability window, achieving stable operation of full cells across wide voltage ranges while maintaining long-term cyclability. By leveraging molecular crowding to modulate solvation structure and hydrogen-bond dynamics, this work establishes a high-performance, reconfigurable solvation network to overcome interfacial challenges in aqueous ZIBs.

items.title: Multi-task learning in battery lifecycle management: From lab to field
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have become indispensable to global electrification and decarbonization in recent years. Accurate, real-time prediction of both internal and external characteristics is crucial for the structural design, efficient management, and safe operation of LIBs in energy storage applications such as electric vehicles, electric aircraft, and smart grids. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in aging mechanisms, multi-modal data, and multi-task learning (MTL) for LIBs. Specifically, the failure pathways linking aging mechanisms, degradation modes, and influencing factors are systematically investigated to establish a physical foundation for model feature construction and task combination design. Subsequently, multi-modal data sources and cross-scale characterization methods for LIBs are addressed to elucidate the mapping relationships between multi-modal data and task patterns, highlighting the significance of open data sharing in advancing fundamental battery research. This study further develops a theoretical framework for battery MTL and systematically elaborates on the main task combination patterns and auxiliary task design solutions. Furthermore, it evaluates the model complexity and deployment costs of different MTL integration paradigms, thereby filling a gap in the review literature in this field. Finally, the key challenges and potential solutions for applying MTL strategies from the laboratory to the field are examined from four perspectives: high-fidelity models, lightweight models, data privacy, and data-mechanism fusion. This review provides comprehensive guidelines for understanding the principles, architecture, methods, and applications of battery MTL strategies.

items.title: Phenothiazine-based π-extended covalent network cathodes for lithium dual-ion batteries with high energy density and fast charging
items.abstract: P-type organic cathodes have shown great promise for lithium dual-ion batteries (LDIBs), yet their practical deployment remains severely constrained by insufficient operating voltages, sluggish ion kinetics, and structural instability under high-rate conditions. Herein, we report a rational molecular design of a phenothiazine-based π-extended covalent network cathode, designated as Poly(3-methyl-7-(13-methyldibenzo[b,i]phenazine-6(13H)-yl)-10-(p-tolyl)-10H-phenothiazine) (PMPPTZ). Distinct from conventional linear analogues, PMPPTZ features a robust conjugated network framework wherein 6,13-dihydrodibenzo[b,j]phenazine (DDPZ) units are covalently bridged by phenothiazine nodes. This unique structure not only extends the π-electron delocalization pathway to enhance electronic conductivity and redox potential, but also constructs an open porous architecture that facilitates rapid ion diffusion. Meanwhile, the incorporation of sulfur atoms further promotes charge delocalization and facilitates electron transport. As a comparison, its linear analogue named Poly(3,10-dimethyl-7-(13-methyldibenzo[b,i]phenazine-6(13H)-yl)-10H-phenothiazine) (PDMPTZ) is synthesized. Comparative electrochemical evaluations demonstrate that PMPPTZ significantly outperforms PDMPTZ, delivering a high energy density of 614 Wh kg−1 and operating at a high rate of 57 C in half cells. The full cells assembled with graphite anodes and PMPPTZ cathodes exhibit a peak discharge capacity of 167 mAh g−1 and an energy density of 564 Wh kg−1cathode, maintaining stability over 1000 cycles.

items.title: Screening and experimental validation of bifunctional organic lithium salts for direct regeneration of spent LiFePO4 cathodes
items.abstract: Direct regeneration of spent LiFePO4 (LFP) cathodes critically depends on the design of effective lithium supplementation agents capable of simultaneously restoring stoichiometry and crystalline integrity. However, conventional lithium sources are constrained by their lack of intrinsic reducibility and carbon coating functionality, necessitating additional reductants and coating precursors that undermine process scalability and cost-efficiency. Herein, we develop a high-throughput molecular screening framework targeting four essential parameters, including molecule weight, intrinsic redox activity, functional-site configuration, and economic feasibility, to identify next-generation bifunctional organic lithium salts for cathode regeneration. This strategy reveals a family of dual-functional compounds exhibiting both strong reducing ability and self-derived carbon-coating capability, enabling concurrent chemical and structural repair of degraded LFP. As a representative case, dilithium salicylate is experimentally validated as a previously unreported bifunctional lithium salt, achieving full restoration of electrochemical kinetics and lattice stability. The regenerated LFP delivers a high specific capacity of 164.9 mAh g–1 at 0.2C and retains 83.7% after 1000 cycles at 5C, while pouch cells sustain 96.6% retention after 500 cycles at 0.5C, demonstrating outstanding practical feasibility. This work establishes a bifunctional molecular design paradigm for scalable and sustainable closed-loop regeneration of LFP cathodes.

items.title: Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) for silicon anodes: From evolution to interface engineering and system-level optimization
items.abstract: Silicon-based anodes, with an exceptionally high theoretical capacity, have emerged as a promising anode candidate for next-generation lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, critical challenges such as substantial volume expansion, unstable soli electrolyte interphase (SEI), irreversible capacity loss, and mechanical degradation significantly hinder their practical deployment. SEI layer plays a decisive role in the chemomechanical failure and stable lithium storage of silicon anodes. The formation and evolution mechanisms of the silicon-based SEI remain insufficiently elucidated, while modification strategies for silicon electrodes often lack systematic, scientific, and comprehensive guidance, posing ongoing research obstacles. Herein, this review systematically outlines the dynamic structural evolution and failure mechanisms of the SEI on silicon-based anodes, with an in-depth analysis of how tailored interfacial engineering can guide SEI growth. Concurrently, the latest research progress on construction of SEI films for stable lithium storage in silicon-based materials is summarized from two dimensions: (i) surface/interface design for electrode materials, encompassing carbon layer interface regulation, metal and its compound coating, and conductive polymer coating; (ii) battery system engineering, including electrolyte optimization, binder design, prelithiation strategies, and solid-state electrolyte optimization. These strategies, aimed at addressing SEI instability, are evaluated through advanced characterization methods. This review assesses the current state of surface/interface engineering for silicon-based materials and offers novel insights and strategies for the future advancement of silicon-based anodes in high-performance lithium-ion batteries, with a focus on the composition and structural optimization of SEI films.

items.title: Structure dependent optimization of pyrrolidinium bromide complexing agents for high energy density zinc–bromine flow batteries
items.abstract: Zinc–bromine flow batteries (ZBFBs) represent a promising architecture for large-scale energy storage owing to their high theoretical energy density and cost-effectiveness. However, their practical implementation is limited by bromine-induced self-discharge, zinc corrosion, and restricted electrolyte concentrations. Here, we report a systematic molecular engineering strategy involving a series of N-alkyl-N-methylpyrrolidinium bromides ([CnMP]Br, n = 2–12) as bromine complexing agents (BCAs). By integrating physicochemical descriptors with complexation readouts, we developed a two-stage screening workflow to identify promising candidates within this homologous series for subsequent flow-cell validation. As the alkyl chain length increased, Br2 sequestration improved, but reaction kinetics were simultaneously impeded. [C4MP]Br was selected as the most balanced BCA, achieving effective bromine regulation at a low additive concentration (0.5 M). A ZBFB employing 4 M ZnBr2 with 0.5 M [C4MP]Br demonstrated stable operation over 225 cycles, maintaining a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% and an energy efficiency of 86%, while delivering a high capacity of 83.6 Ah L−1. Under extreme conditions (6 M ZnBr2, 80% state-of-charge), a mixed-BCA electrolyte delivered 229 Wh L−1 over 12 cycles, showing improved short-term performance compared with the tested single-BCA formulations under the same conditions. This work presents a practical electrolyte optimization strategy for pyrrolidinium-bromide-based ZBFBs under high-concentration conditions while highlighting the need for further improvements in efficiency and durability.

items.title: The significant in-plane heterogeneity of cathode performance in aged lithium iron phosphate batteries: Modeling and mitigation method
items.abstract: Redox reactions in lithium-ion batteries exhibit multiscale heterogeneity arising from intrinsic material variations and evolving structural defects, which profoundly influence cell performance and safety. While electrode architecture and cycling conditions are often considered the dominant sources of both in-plane and through-thickness nonuniformity, this study demonstrates that aged lithium iron phosphate (LFP) electrodes exhibit a distinct, location-dependent in-plane electrochemical heterogeneity governed by the intrinsic degradation of the active material. Through combined electrochemical experiments and detailed material characterization, we reveal a spatially symmetric variation in-plane performance that correlates strongly with microstructural defects, such as particle cracks and voids. Guided by these observations, we develop an electrochemical model that quantitatively captures the evolution of in-plane heterogeneity and shows that such variations give rise to pronounced nonuniformity in lateral current distribution during cycling. By incorporating mechanical stress into the model, we further demonstrate that appropriately tailored compressive stress profiles can substantially homogenize the in-plane current distribution, mitigating the adverse effects of aging-induced defects. This work provides a mechanistic framework and predictive modeling tool for optimizing electrode design and operating conditions, enabling safer, more durable, and higher-performance next-generation batteries.

items.title: Towards sustainable battery management: Developing battery health estimation models from only incomplete charging curve
items.abstract: Accurately estimating the degradation state of energy storage devices such as lithium-ion batteries is imperative towards the goal of carbon neutrality. Despite advancements in machine learning in this area, a persistent and yet overlooked challenge is the demand for high-quality degradation data comprising complete charging curves for model training. Generating such data requires extensive battery ageing tests, which are resource-intensive and environmentally costly. Here, we introduce battery ageing tag-free training (BATT), a novel approach designed to train degradation models using only incomplete charging curves, which are commonly available in routine battery operations. BATT adopts a self-supervised strategy to extract degradation knowledge without relying on manually labelled state-of-health (SOH) data, thereby substantially reducing experimental and environmental burdens. Our BATT is validated on four distinct battery degradation datasets from 84 commercial lithium-ion batteries, encompassing over 26,000 ageing cycles under various conditions. Compared to traditional methods, which fail to work in the absence of SOH labels derived from complete charging curves, BATT provides highly accurate predictions. Using only incomplete charging curves covering 2/3 of the full voltage range for training, we achieve root mean squared errors of <6.5 mAh, 6.3 mAh, 16.9 mAh, and 6.9 mAh in the maximum capacity estimation of 0.74-Ah, 3.5-Ah, 2.0-Ah, and 2.5-Ah batteries, respectively. By leveraging data already available from operational systems, our approach eliminates the need for thousands of days of battery tests, offering a pathway toward more sustainable and scalable battery management.

items.title: A novel synergistic optimization strategy for tuning heavy rare earth diffusion behavior to significantly enhance the coercivity of Nd-Fe-B magnets
items.abstract: The grain boundary diffusion (GBD) process is a critical technology for enhancing the coercivity of Nd-Fe-B magnets. However, this technology suffers from limited heavy rare earth (HRE) diffusion depth and excessive thickness of the HRE-rich shell structure on the magnet surface, which severely hinders further improvements in both HRE utilization efficiency and coercivity. This study developed a novel optimization strategy for HRE diffusion in Nd-Fe-B magnets, leveraging the synergistic effects of different elements. Aluminum (Al) was utilized to inhibit the chemically induced liquid film migration (CILFM) mechanism, thereby preventing excessive shell thickening and reducing HRE consumption near the magnet surface. Simultaneously, indium (In), an element with high mobility, was introduced into grain boundaries to lower the activation energy for Tb diffusion, consequently increasing its diffusion depth. Through a simple one-step diffusion process, Tb65Cu10Al10In15 diffusion source achieved a coercivity increment of 10.51 kOe in a 6 mm-thick Nd-Fe-B magnet with low HRE usage (0.3 wt.% Tb), representing the highest coercivity enhancement for GBD thick magnets using a low-HRE-content diffusion source. Micromagnetic simulations demonstrated that appropriately reducing the HRE-rich shell thickness while increasing the diffusion depth was more effective for efficient utilization of HRE and enhancing coercivity, consistent with experimental results. This work confirmed the inhibitory effect of Al on CILFM and explored the positive role of in GBD Nd-Fe-B magnets. The synergistic optimization effects promoted deeper Tb diffusion, forming a more uniform shell structure and optimized grain boundaries, thereby significantly enhancing coercivity. This research paves the way for designing high-performance, cost-effective Nd-Fe-B magnets with improved HRE utilization.

items.title: Bioinspired inosculation of heterogeneous carbon network structures to prompt heat conduction
items.abstract: It is a common approach to construct material structures using high-aspect-ratio units for specific functionalities. However, the realisation of structural and functional continuity from individual building blocks remains challenging. Inspired by the inosculation of twinned-trunk in nature and the capability of resource sharing and exchange, a new strategy for assembling porous 3D carbon networks is developed in this study. In this design, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were in-situ grown on carbon fibres (CFs) to initiate nano-branching by chemical vapour deposition, and pyrolytic carbon (PyC) was subsequently deposited on the CNTs and CFs to form an interconnection between adjacent fibres. This inosculation structure, mimicking the cellular fusion between trunks and branches, established continuous interconnections between independent carbon phases. As proof of resource sharing with functional continuity, the inosculated heterogeneous carbon network was incorporated into polydimethylsiloxane matrices after graphitisation for prompting heat conduction. The fabricated composites demonstrated substantially improved thermal conductivity, attaining a through-plane value of 18.8 W/(m K) at 21.4 vol% carbon material loading. This inosculation assembly strategy provides a transformative paradigm for constructing advanced functional materials requiring continuous interconnected 3D networks.
